title: KMRD materials research data schema
description: working copy for version 2026-01 starting from "kmrd-schema v2025-02"; Materials Research Data Schema (version 2026-01) developed by the Expert Committee for Materials R&D Data Standardization in the National Center of Materials Research Data (NCMRD) of Korea

dataset ID.$comment: this is required to exclusively identify the materials in this dataset. Partial data of the materials can be thus integrated into one complete dataset.
dataset ID.description: ID for dataset, automatically assigned by the KMDS data platform

dataset name.description: name of the data set, named by data provider; This is your own unique data or specimen identifier. With this text string alone, you should be able to identify the materials (system) in your own internal data management system.

data classification.description: classification code for relevant fields of science and technology announced by Ministry of Science and ICT of KOREA (https://www.law.go.kr)

data generation date.description: date when the data is added to the present database or data lake

data source.description: source information of the data, such as lab log, source publication, related projects, DOI of data, lead author, and publication date if the data is extracted from a publication; The DOI number referring to the published paper or dataset where the data can be found. If the data is unpublished, enter “Unpublished”; lead author is the surname of the first author. If several authors, end with et al. If the DOI number is given correctly, this will be extracted automatically from www.crossref.org ; publication date will be extracted automatically from www.crossref.org if the DOI number is given correctly.
examples: extracted from Acta Mater vol 13, page 2089 (2000)

name.description: contributor's name in the form of "[last name], [first name]"

position @@08.description: Position or role of the contributor

affiliation.description: contributor's affiliation (institute's name and further description of working place)

researcher number.description: contributor’s researcher number ID in Integrated R&D Information System of Korea (https://iris.go.kr); only applied for Korean researchers

keywords.description: keywords representing the data set or material type and description, at least 3 keywords should be provided

embargo.description: date when allowing open access of the data

note on data @@03.description: additional information or comments about the data
examples: Outlier removed due to device failure, initial measurement

materials.description: inherent data of material that composed of the material system; this is array of n materials defined by the material_id

id.description: id of materials inside of the dataset, that is to be used for defining materials system

universal specimen identifier.$comment: this is required to exclusively identify the materials in this dataset. Partial data of the materials can be thus integrated into one complete dataset.
universal specimen identifier.description: unique identifier of material specimen; automatically assigned as "dataset ID"-"material id"

name.description: description of materials according to customary usage, designation system, composition, supplier, brand name, polymer name based on IUPAC recommendation (https://iupac.org/polymer-edu/polymer-naming/), etc.

physicochemical information.description: physical and chemical information of material

doping.description: dopant and its dose for modifying structure and properties of materials

level.description: doping level as the dose of each element in the form of dictionary {"dopant": dose in atom per square cm"}

uniformity @@10.description: URI of image file showing degree of uniformity of doping concentration distribution within a wafer.

composition.description: composition of materials

value.description: composition value in dictionary form; {"constituent": concentration,....}

unit.description: unit of the composition value in at.% or wt.%

oxidation state.description: the number of electrons that an atom is considered to have lost or gained relative to its neutral elemental state, assuming that all bonds are purely ionic; data in dictionary form {"constituent": "oxidation state",....}

density.description: mass per unit volume of a substance

pellet density @@02.description: The mass of compressed pellet of powder materials divided by the volume of the pellet

ligand exchange degree @@03.description: the ratio to which the original surface-bound ligands on nanomaterials have been replaced with new ligands, typically determined by FTIR or other spectroscopic analyses
ligand exchange degree @@03.alias: surface ligand exchange degree; ligand replacement degree

hybrid bonds.description: fraction of s-p hybrid bond in the materials. This fraction is dependent on the materials process and is significant in understanding materials structure and properties in covalent bonded materials composed of C, N, O, B, Be, P, or S

sp fraction.description: quantity of sp hybridization in percent; In chemistry, hybrid bonds are formed by hybridizing orbitals. sp hybrid bonds forms a linear geometry when one s orbital mixes with one p orbital forming two equivalent sp hybrid orbitals

sp2 fraction.description: quantity of sp2 hybridization in percent

sp3 fraction.description: quantity of sp3 hybridization in percent

molecule.description: molecules as the unit of materials; the smallest structural unit of a polymer that retains the chemical composition and connectivity of the repeating segments in the polymer chain

CAS number.description: a numeri(c)al designation assigned to chemical substances by the U.S. Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS)

chemical formula.description: the molecular formula about the chemical proportions of atoms that constitute whole number ratio of atoms present in a compound or constitutional unit

formula weight.description: sum of the standard atomic weights of the constituent elements, each multiplied by its stoichiometric coefficient in the formula, expressed in grams per mole (g/mol)

SMILES.description: human-readable string notation for describing the structure of molecules, simplified molecular-input line-entry system

structural formula.description: the molecular formula about a typographic system arose to describe organic structures in a line of functional group

plasticizer.description: a substance added to a material, typically a polymer, to make it softer, more flexible, and easier to handle. Plasticizers reduce intermolecular forces within the polymer matrix, decreasing the glass transition temperature and improving processability.

classification.description: 22 classifications based on the chemical structure of constitutional repeating unit of the polymer and related categories (Ref: https://polymer.nims.go.jp/PoLyInfo/guide/en/term_polymer.html)

degree of polymerization.description: number of each monomers contained in one polymer chain or polymer molecule; it is calculated for homopolymer by dividing the molecular weight of the polymer by the molecular weight of the repeat unit.

dispersity.description: ratio of the weight-average molecular weight to the number-average molecular weight; dispersity D = (M_w) / (M_n), where M_w is the weight-average molecular weight and M_n the number-average molecular weight
dispersity.alias: polydispersity index; PDI; molecular weight distribution

GPC (SEC) peak molar mass.description: molecular weight obtained from the peak value refers to the maximum point of gel permeation chromatographic (GPC) peak or size exclusion chromatographic (SEC) peak; the peak value provides the information about the molecular weight and distribution of polymers.

number-average molar mass.description: number-average molecular weights of materials; the average molecular weight of a polymer sample based on the number of molecules; M_n = sum{(N_i) x (M_i)} / sum {(N_i)}, where N_i is the number of molecules of species i and M_i the molecular weight of species i.

viscosity-average molar mass.description: a measure to characterize the molecular weight of a polymer based on its viscosity; particularly useful for understanding the flow behavior of polymer solutions and melts; M_v = K x [eta], where K is a constant that depends on the specific polymer and solvent used and [eta] the intrinsic viscosity of the polymer solution, which is a measure of how the viscosity of a solution changes with concentration.

weight-average molar mass.description: weight-average molecular weights of materials; a measure of the average molecular weight of a polymer sample, taking into account the weight of each molecule; M_w = sum{(w_i) x (M_i)} / sum{(w_i)}, where w_i is the weight of species i and M_i the molecular weight of species i

z-average molar mass.description: average molecular weight that gives greater weight to larger molecules, making it particularly sensitive to high molecular weight species within the distribution; M_z= sum{(M_i)^2 x (N_i)} / sum{(M_i) x (N_i)}, where M_i is the molecular weight of species i and N_i the number of molecules of species i

architecture.description: molecular structure regarding atom connectivity and arrangement; structural information when the polymer chain is seen within the range that is bigger than the constitutional repeating unit
architecture.alias: molecular structure; molecular arrangement; chain architecture

homogeneity.description: monomer homogeneity of the polymer chain

end groups.description: the chemical group or functional group present at the two ends of a polymer chain, which significantly influence the reactivity, properties and degradation of the polymer

branch molecule.description: a molecular branch or chain connected to the main polymer backbone; a molecular chain that extends from the main polymer backbone chain; it is a deviation from a perfectly linear structure.

number of branches.description: average number of branches attached to a single polymer molecule

degree of branching.description: percentage of the number of branches present in a polymer in its total number of repeating units

average branch length.description: length of the polymer chains between branching points

branching density.description: number of branches per unit length of the main polymer chain

branching index.description: the ratio between the radius of gyration of a branched polymer and that of a linear polymer of the same molar mass (range : 0~1)

cross-linking density.description: The number of cross-links per unit volume in a polymer network, representing the degree of interconnection between polymer chains through chemical bonds. It quantifies the three-dimensional network structure formed when polymer chains are linked together by covalent or ionic bonds.
cross-linking density.alias: network density; degree of cross-linking; cross-link density

cross-linking agent.description: A substance that promotes or regulates the formation of covalent bonds between polymer chains, resulting in a three-dimensional network structure. These agents react with functional groups on the polymer chains to create bridges or cross-links that connect separate polymer molecules.
cross-linking agent.alias: cross-linker; curing agent; hardener; vulcanizing agent; cross-linking additive; reticulating agent
examples: Epoxy hardeners (amine or anhydride-based curing agents)
Ethylene glycol dimethacrylate (EGDMA - crosslinking of methacrylate polymers)

core.description: central part of star polymer that acts as the central junction point from which all the polymer arms radiate outwards

arm number.description: number of linear polymer chains that radiate from the central core

arm length.description: length of each individual polymer arm

number of generation.description: total number of generation to indicate the level of branching in a dendrimer. It starts from generation 0 (the core) and increases with each layer of branching

core.description: central part of star polymer that acts as the central junction point from which all the polymer arms radiate outwards

branches.description: average number and length of branches in each generation

length.description: average length of branches in each generation

degree of ladderization.description: The fraction (or percentage) of the polymer backbone that has successfully formed the complete double-stranded ladder structure via cyclization reaction, without open-chain defects

persistence length.description: A measure of the stiffness of a polymer chain, defined as the length over which the direction of the polymer backbone segments remains correlated (i.e., the chain behaves like a rigid rod)

dihedral angle.description: The angle between planes defined by the backbone atoms, quantifying the twist or contortion of the ladder structure. It determines the planarity of the ribbon-like chain

fractional free volume.description: The ratio of the specific free volume (empty space not occupied by the polymer chains) to the total specific volume of the polymer material; FFV=(V_sp-1.34V_vdw)/V_sp

name.description: conventional name of backbone molecule of the bottlebrush polymer

degree of polymerization.description: number of repeating units in the backbone

dispersity.description: dispersity of backbone; ratio of the weight-average molecular weight to the number-average molecular weight;

name.example: PDMS; PBA; PEG; POx; PCB; PNIPAM; PDMEAEMA; PLA; PS

degree of polymerization.description: number of each monomers contained in one polymer chain or polymer molecule; it is calculated for homopolymer by dividing the molecular weight of the polymer by the molecular weight of the repeat unit.

dispersity.description: dispersity of side chain; ratio of the weight-average molecular weight to the number-average molecular weight;

grafting density.description: number of side chains per backbone repeat unit

composition.description: molar percent of each comonomer type in a copolymer chain in dictionary form {"monomer": "mol. %",...}

band gap correction.alias: band gap error correction; scissor correction

architecture.description:
The cell architecture with respect to the direction of current flow and the order in which layers are deposited. The two most common are nip (also referred to as normal) and pin (also referred to as inverted) but there are also a few others, e.g. Back contacted 
• nip architecture means that the electrons are collected at the substrate side. The typical examples is when a TiO2 electron selective contact is deposited between the perovskite and the substrate (e.g. SLG | FTO | TiO2-c |Perovskite | …)   
• pin architecture means that it instead is the holes that are collected at the substrate side. The typical examples is when a PEDOT:PSS hole selective contact is deposited between the perovskite and the substrate (e.g. SLG | FTO | PEDOT:PSS |Perovskite | …)

additional layer front.description: functional layer below the substrate, or on the opposite side of the substrate from with respect to the device layers

material.description: Material of the additional layer front. The layer can be a stack of layers made of material_(n) defined in the materials section. Every layer in the stack should be separated by a space, a vertical bar, and a space, i.e. (' | ').

thickness.description:
Thickness of the layers in the additional layer front. 
• Thickness of each layer in the stack should be separated by a space, a vertical bar, and a space, i.e. (' | '). 
• The layers must line up with the previous material field.
• Every layer in the stack have a thickness. If it is unknown, state this as ‘nan’
• If there are uncertainties, state the best estimate, e.g. write 100 and not 90-110

function.description:
The function of the additional layers front
• The function must line up with the previous material field.
• Every layer should be separated by a space, a vertical bar, and a space, i.e. (‘ | ‘)
• If a layer has more than one function, e.g. A and B, list the functions in order and separate them with semicolons, as in (A; B)

substrate.description: configurational information of the substrate. With the substrate, we refer to any layer below the electron transport layer in a nip-device, and any layer below the hole transport layer in a pin-device. The substrate can be a stack of layer of material_(n)

material.description: Material of the substrate. The substrate can be a stack of layers made of material_(n) defined in the materials section. Every layer in the stack should be separated by a space, a vertical bar, and a space, i.e. (' | ').

thickness.description:
Thickness of the layers of the substrate. 
• Thickness of each layer in the stack should be separated by a space, a vertical bar, and a space, i.e. (' | '). 
• The layers must line up with the previous material field.
• Every layer in the stack have a thickness. If it is unknown, state this as ‘nan’
• If there are uncertainties, state the best estimate, e.g write 100 and not 90-110

area.description: The total area in cm2 of the substrate over which the perovskite is deposited. This may be significantly larger than the cell area

atmosphere.description:
The atmosphere in which the sample was stored between the device finalization and the IV measurement.
• If the atmosphere is a mixture of different gases, e.g. A and B, list the gases in alphabetic order and separate them with semicolons, as in (A; B)
• “Dry air” represent air with low relative humidity but where the relative humidity is not known
• “Ambient” represent air where the relative humidity is not known. For ambient conditions where the relative humidity is known, state this as “Air”
• “Vacuum” (of unspecified pressure) is for this purpose considered as an atmospheric gas
• If the atmosphere has changed during the storing time, separate the different atmospheres by a double forward angel bracket with one blank space on both sides (‘ >> ‘)

relative humidity.description:
the relative humidity in the atmosphere in which the sample was stored between the device finalization and the IV measurement.
• Relative humidity is the actual amount of water vapor in the air compared to the total amount of vapor that can exist in the air at its current temperature
• If the relative humidity has changed during the storing time, separate the different relative humidity by a double forward angel bracket with one blank space on both sides (‘ >> ‘)
• If the relative humidity is not known, stat that as ‘nan’
• For values with uncertainties, state the best estimate, e.g. write 35 and not 30-40.

simulator classification.description:
Classification of the light source/solar simulator used during the IV measurement according to the IEC 60904-9 Ed.3
• A three-letter code consisting of A+, A, B, and C. The order of the letters represents the quality of: spectral match, spatial non-uniformity, and temporal instability of the light source/solar simulator.

light.description: data of the characteristics of light illuminated during JV measurement

intensity.description:
The radiant power per unit area of light incident on a surface. In the case of the IV measurement of a photovoltaic device, it means the irradiance of the light source/solar simulator used during the measurement.
• If there are uncertainties, only state the best estimate, e.g. write 100 and not 90-100.
• Standard AM 1.5 illumination correspond to 100 mW/cm2
• If you need to convert from illumination given in lux; at 550 nm, 1 mW/cm2 corresponds to 6830 lux. Be aware that the conversion change with the spectrum used. As a rule of thumb for general fluorescent/LED light sources, around 0.31mW corresponded to 1000 lux. If your light intensity is measured in lux, it probably means that your light spectra deviates quite a lot from AM 1.5, wherefore it is very important that you also specify the light spectra in the next column.

type of spectrum.description: The spectral type of the light source/solar simulator used during the IV measurement

wavelength range.description:

• If there are uncertainties, only state the best estimate, e.g. write 100 and not 90-100.
• State unknown values as ‘nan’

The number of cells the reported stability data is based on.

• The category Solar simulator should only be used when you do not really know which type of light source you have in your solar simulator.

simulator classification.description:
Classification of the light source/solar simulator used during the stability measurement according to the IEC 60904-9 Ed.3
• A three-letter code consisting of A+, A, B, and C. The order of the letters represents the quality of: spectral match, spatial non-uniformity, and temporal instability of the light source/solar simulator.

light.description: data of the characteristics of light illuminated during stability measurement

intensity.description:
The radiant power per unit area of light incident on a surface. In the case of the stability measurement of a photovoltaic device, it means the irradiance of the light source/solar simulator used during the stability measurement.
• If there are uncertainties, only state the best estimate, e.g. write 100 and not 90-100.
• Standard AM 1.5 illumination correspond to 100 mW/cm2
• If you need to convert from illumination given in lux; at 550 nm, 1 mW cm^{-2} corresponds to 6830 lux. Be aware that the conversion change with the spectrum used. As a rule of thumb for general fluorescent/LED light sources, around 0.31mW corresponded to 1000 lux. If your light intensity is measured in lux, it probably means that your light spectra deviates quite a lot from AM 1.5, wherefore it is very important that you also specify the light spectra in the next column.

type of spectrum.description: The spectral type of the light source/solar simulator used during the stability measurement

wavelength range.description:

• State unknown values as ‘nan’

load condition.description:
The load situation of the illumination during the stability measurement.

• If the situation periodically is interrupted by IV-measurements, continue to consider the load condition as constant
• If there is a cycling between dark and light, state this as ‘Cycled’
• If the illumination varies in an uncontrolled way, state this as ‘Uncontrolled’
• This category was included after the projects initial phase wherefor the list of reported categories is 
short. Thus, be prepared to expand the given list of alternatives in the data template.

triboelectric measurement ##6.description: Experimental evaluation of electrical signals generated by contact and separation or sliding between materials to characterize triboelectric charge generation, energy-harvesting performance, and when applicable, temperature or frictional-heat effects. This section also covers standardized triboelectric charge density (TECD) measurements using a liquid metal electrode, in operando measurements correlating frictional heat and temperature with triboelectric charge, thin-film coated triboelectric nanogenerators (TENG) (e.g., DLC, MoS2, MXene coatings on PTFE or other polymers), and various TENG working modes (vertical contact–separation, in-plane sliding, freestanding, single- and double-electrode configurations).

instrument.description: Device for measuring triboelectrically generated voltage, current, and charge during material contact–separation or sliding, optionally combined with friction, wear, and temperature measurement. It can include standardized TECD systems with liquid metal electrodes, in operando frictional-heat setups, or thin-film (DLC/MoS2/MXene) based TENG apparatus in contact-separation, sliding, freestanding, and rotational modes.

excess.description:
Components that are in excess in the material synthesis. E.g. to form stoichiometric perovskite MAPbI3, PbI2 and MAI are mixed in the proportions 1:1. If one of them are in excess compared to the other, then that component is considered to be in excess. This information can be inferred from data entered on the concentration for all reaction solutions but this gives a convenient shorthand filtering option. 
• If more than one component is in excess, order them in alphabetic order and separate them by semicolons.
• It there are no components that are in excess, write Stoichiometric

The age of the solutions
• As a general guideline, the age refers to the time from the preparation of the final precursor mixture to the reaction procedure.

• For solutions that is stored a long time, an order of magnitude estimate is adequate.

state.description:
The physical state of the precursor
• The three basic categories are Solid/Liquid/Gas
• Most cases are clear cut, e.g. spin-coating involves species in solution and evaporation involves species in gas phase. For less clear-cut cases, consider where the reaction really is happening as in:
o For a spray-coating procedure, it is droplets of liquid that enters the substrate (thus a liquid phase reaction) 
o For sputtering and thermal evaporation, it is species in gas phase that reaches the substrate (thus a gas phase reaction)
• This category was included after the projects initial phase wherefor the list of reported categories is short. Thus, be prepared to expand the given list of alternatives in the data template.

Rapid cooling of the specimen from high temperature for manipulating microstructure or crystallinity of materials.

In perovskite synthesis process, quenching is a measure to discontinuously accelerate the crystallization 
• The most common case is the antisolvent treatment where a volume of a solvent in which the perovskite is not soluble is poured on the substrate during spin coating.
• The same effect can also be achieved by blowing a gas on the sample
• If the sample quickly after spin coating is subjected to a vacuum, this also counts as quenched induced crystallization

• For solutions that is stored a long time, an order of magnitude estimate is adequate.

state.description:
The physical state of the precursor
• The three basic categories are Solid/Liquid/Gas
• Most cases are clear cut, e.g. spin-coating involves species in solution and evaporation involves species in gas phase. For less clear-cut cases, consider where the reaction really is happening as in:
o For a spray-coating procedure, it is droplets of liquid that enters the substrate (thus a liquid phase reaction) 
o For sputtering and thermal evaporation, it is species in gas phase that reaches the substrate (thus a gas phase reaction)
• This category was included after the projects initial phase wherefor the list of reported categories is short. Thus, be prepared to expand the given list of alternatives in the data template.
